If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative over 3 consecutive days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% starting at day 10 of the 30-day window.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but recent price action shows downward momentum, reduce forecast by 1.0–2.0% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to align with trend reversal.  
If sentiment is negative but recent price action shows upward momentum, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture reversal potential.
